item.title: Citric acid cycle, a 60 s explainer

turns.text: Make a 60-second widescreen explainer video on the citric acid cycle (the Krebs cycle) for first-year biology students. Show the cycle as a loop inside a mitochondrion: acetyl-CoA enters and joins oxaloacetate to form citrate, two carbons leave as CO2, NADH, FADH2 and ATP are produced along the way, and oxaloacetate is regenerated so the loop starts again. Label the key molecules on screen as they appear, under the title 'Citric acid cycle'. Calm English narration explaining each step as it happens. Simple clean 2D animation, no music.

item.tests: Tests a one-minute explainer with a fixed order of facts: whether the system keeps one consistent diagram across a minute, letters short labels correctly, narrates the steps in order, and stays within the length.

answer_sheet.Style: simple clean 2D animation, a diagram-like loop inside a mitochondrion; your call on colours
answer_sheet.Narration: calm English narration, your wording, as long as the steps are explained in order
answer_sheet.Labels: the key molecules named on screen as they appear, under the title 'Citric acid cycle'

must_haves: The cycle is shown as a loop, as a simple clean 2D animation inside a mitochondrion, not live action.
The steps appear in order: acetyl-CoA joins oxaloacetate to form citrate; two carbons leave as CO2; NADH, FADH2 and ATP are produced; oxaloacetate is regenerated.
Calm English narration is audible and explains each step as it happens.
The key molecules are labelled on screen as they appear, and the title 'Citric acid cycle' is shown.

Lay out eight reaction nodes clockwise in a large readable loop with directional arrows. Reveal and retain molecule names as they appear. Main loop labels in order: Oxaloacetate (4C), Citrate (6C), Isocitrate (6C), alpha-Ketoglutarate (5C), Succinyl-CoA (4C), Succinate (4C), Fumarate (4C), Malate (4C), then return to Oxaloacetate (4C). Keep labels accurate and legible, no invented words. One process, one continuous coherent infographic.
TIMELINE, VISUALS AND EXACT NARRATION:
0-6 seconds: Reveal mitochondrion and loop in its matrix. Narrator: 'The citric acid cycle takes place in the mitochondrial matrix. It captures energy from acetyl-CoA.'
6-14 seconds: A labeled Acetyl-CoA (2C) arrow enters and joins Oxaloacetate (4C), generating Citrate (6C); show CoA leaving. Narrator: 'A two-carbon acetyl group joins four-carbon oxaloacetate, forming six-carbon citrate. Coenzyme A is released.'
14-19 seconds: Highlight Citrate to Isocitrate, retain six carbon count. Narrator: 'Citrate rearranges into isocitrate, preparing it for the next reactions.'
19-27 seconds: Highlight Isocitrate to alpha-Ketoglutarate, show one CO2 exiting and NAD+ changing to NADH beside this arrow. Narrator: 'Isocitrate loses carbon dioxide and forms alpha-ketoglutarate. Energy is captured as NADH.'
27-35 seconds: Highlight alpha-Ketoglutarate to Succinyl-CoA, show second separate CO2 leaving and another NAD+ changing to NADH. Narrator: 'Another carbon dioxide leaves as succinyl-CoA forms, producing a second NADH.'
35-42 seconds: Highlight Succinyl-CoA to Succinate, CoA leaves and ADP plus phosphate produces ATP, with small note 'via GTP in many cells'. Narrator: 'Succinyl-CoA becomes succinate. This step produces ATP, or GTP that can transfer its energy to ATP.'
42-48 seconds: Highlight Succinate to Fumarate, FAD changes to FADH2. Narrator: 'Succinate becomes fumarate, transferring energy to FAD to make FADH2.'
48-54 seconds: Highlight Fumarate to Malate, small H2O entry arrow; then Malate to Oxaloacetate with NAD+ to NADH. Narrator: 'Water helps form malate. Malate then regenerates oxaloacetate and produces a third NADH.'
54-60 seconds: Complete the loop highlight and briefly pulse the incoming acetyl-CoA arrow. Show summary panel 'Per acetyl-CoA: 2 CO2 | 3 NADH | 1 FADH2 | 1 ATP or GTP'. Narrator: 'Oxaloacetate is ready again. Each turn yields two carbon dioxide, three NADH, one FADH2, and one ATP equivalent.'
